security.title: Missing Initialization of a Variable
security.description: The product does not initialize critical variables, which causes the execution environment to use unexpected values.

evidence.explanation: HomeController declares the static BlobContainerClient field without initialization at line 47. It is only assigned in Index at line 65, while UploadAsync, DeleteImage, and DeleteAll use it without checking or ensuring initialization (lines 108, 135, and 158), so direct requests can operate on a null resource.

security.title: Use of Uninitialized Variable
security.description: The code uses a variable that has not been initialized, leading to unpredictable or unintended results.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync uses the static blobContainer field at line 108, but it is initialized only as a side effect of calling Index at line 65. A direct upload request before Index executes dereferences the uninitialized (null) field.

security.title: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
security.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync copies Request.Files.Count into fileCount at line 102 and uses that unvalidated request-controlled value as the loop bound at line 106. There is no per-request file-count limit in application code, so a request containing many files can trigger an excessive number of upload iterations.

security.title: Improper Initialization
security.description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.

evidence.explanation: HomeController does not initialize the static blobContainer field at declaration (line 47); its initialization occurs only in Index (line 65), while upload and delete actions assume it is ready. A request invoking one of those actions first encounters an uninitialized storage client.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: HomeController stores BlobContainerClient in a static field at line 47, assigns it in Index at line 65, and reads it in concurrent request actions (lines 75, 108, 135, 158) without synchronization. Concurrent MVC requests can access the shared field while it is being initialized or reassigned.

security.title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
security.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.Index calls CreateIfNotExistsAsync(PublicAccessType.Blob) at line 66, configuring uploaded blobs for anonymous public read access. This exposes gallery content to anyone with a blob URL, without a configurable privacy or access-control check.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The upload, individual delete, and bulk-delete actions perform security-relevant operations but do not record audit events. Their catch blocks only place exception messages and stack traces in ViewData (for example lines 114-118 and 140-144); there is no logging of actors, target blobs, or outcomes.

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes the client-controlled HttpPostedFileBase.FileName to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path) at line 109. The path-based overload reads that path from the server filesystem; a crafted relative or absolute filename can therefore cause a server file to be uploaded to the public blob container. The upload also accepts arbitrary file types without validating content or extension (lines 101-109).

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: HomeController.UploadAsync passes the client-controlled HttpPostedFileBase.FileName to BlobClient.UploadAsync(string path) at line 109. The path-based overload reads that path from the server filesystem; a crafted relative or absolute filename can therefore cause a server file to be uploaded to the public blob container. security.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
security.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

evidence.explanation: In DisplayFilesToUpload, line 80 concatenates the selected file name (file.name) directly into an HTML string, and line 85 assigns that string to innerHTML. A specially named local file can therefore inject markup or script into the gallery page.
